meta.title: Four Students Undercut A $140 Billion Eyewear Industry By $400 A Pair
meta.hook: Warby Parker attacked eyewear pricing by removing a layer most customers never saw: the traditional middleman.
meta.description: In 2010, four Wharton students founded Warby Parker after noticing eyewear giants marked up frames costing around $8 to manufacture into $300 to $500 retail prices. By designing frames in-house and selling direct to consumers online starting at $95, they bypassed the traditional wholesale and licensing chain. Warby Parker now holds roughly 7% of the US eyewear market.

scenes.narration: Warby Parker attacked eyewear pricing by removing a layer most customers never saw: the traditional middleman.

visual.visual_intent: A single pair of glasses frames lit dramatically on a dark surface, macro detail, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: hook: the markup gap, widely reported industry figure

scenes.narration: Founded in twenty ten, the company began as an online brand selling prescription glasses directly to consumers.

visual.visual_intent: Young founders working around a laptop and sketches, natural window light, documentary style
visual.decision_reason: the founding origin, corroborated across multiple business press retrospectives

scenes.narration: It designed its own frames, controlled its brand, and avoided relying entirely on traditional wholesale distribution.

visual.query: supply chain diagram multiple steps screen

visual.decision_reason: explains the old cost structure being bypassed

scenes.narration: Its Home Try-On program mailed five frames to customers, solving a basic problem with buying glasses online.

visual.visual_intent: A laptop screen showing an online eyewear checkout, warm home setting, natural light, cinematic

scenes.narration: Warby Parker's filing says glasses started at ninety-five dollars, including prescription lenses, using simple unified pricing.

visual.query: price tag ninety five dollars glasses

scenes.narration: The idea was not merely cheaper frames. It was rebuilding the path from design to customer and keeping control of that relationship.
